The Microsoft driver package declares a dependency on openssl, and the served openssl 3.5.9-r0 requires exactly libssl3=3.5.9-r0 and libcrypto3=3.5.9-r0, so app/infra/locks/backend-alpine-packages.lock moves the three packages to 3.5.9-r0 (Apache-2.0; .apk SHA-256 bytes observed from dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org on 2026-10-02, file sizes equal to the APKINDEX records). OpenSSL 3.5.9 (upstream release 2026-09-29) is a security patch release whose most severe fix is High; Alpine aports commit adcf4978 (main/openssl: security upgrade to 3.5.9) names the thirteen CVEs recorded in the exception. OSV queries for Alpine:v3.23 openssl 3.5.9-r0 and Alpine:v3.24 pcre2 10.49-r0 on 2026-10-02 returned no advisory. The three releases are younger than 30 days and are recorded as security exceptions; the reviewed inventory grows from 103 to 105 coordinates. Compatibility on 2026-10-02: the frontend and backend release images build without cache in connected mode for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (pcre2 10.48-r0 -> 10.49-r0; libcrypto3 and libssl3 3.5.8-r0 -> 3.5.9-r0, openssl 3.5.9-r0). Trivy reports 0 findings at every severity for the frontend image on both architectures and 0 operating-system package findings for the backend image. The backend image still reports 1 CRITICAL and 9 HIGH Python package findings on both architectures, which this change does not address: PyJWT 2.13.0 (1 CRITICAL and 5 HIGH, fixed in 2.14.0; the kt-scaffold profile pin) and msgpack 1.1.2, setuptools 70.3.0 and urllib3 2.7.0 (4 HIGH), which the pinned Python base image itself carries. The frontend image served the application with HTTP 200 as user 101 on a read-only root file system with every capability dropped (nginx/1.31.6). On both backend images Python 3.14.7 links OpenSSL 3.5.9, unixODBC registers 'ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server', a pyodbc connection attempt reaches the driver (login timeout against a closed port) and pip check reports no broken requirement. tests/infra/local-egress.test.sh passed, including the gate configuration check on the new image. scripts/quality-gate.sh all passed on a separate Compose project with the development image rebuilt without cache from the new lock (backend lint, strict types, 726 unit and PostgreSQL integration tests, database validation, OpenAPI contract, frontend lint, build, 144 tests and generated types, governance drift and Helm render). Limits: the local Compose reverse proxy and the local-egress gate run the base image without a build and keep pcre2 10.48-r0; the proxy listens on the loopback address only and the gate publishes no port. Alpine does not keep superseded package versions, so a locked version stops downloading once its successor is published and the lock then has to move. This is a local build and scan; it is not evidence of the GitHub image publication or of the nonprod deployment.
